overall: NYC is already at 82°F by 8:50 AM with an Extreme Heat Warning in effect for Manhattan, Bronx, and Brooklyn, suggesting a very hot day underway. The warming rate has decelerated from +2.0°F/hr (2-hour average) to +1.1°F/hr most recently, which is normal for this hour but means the pace of heating is tapering. Afternoon thunderstorms (60% chance from 2–5 PM) pose a meaningful cap risk on the daily high by triggering an early evaporative cooling crash before the full peak is reached.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in rough agreement on an extremely hot day (GFS 103.3°F, ECMWF 98.0°F, HRRR 98.9°F, NBM 96.2°F), all well above the NWS official call of ~95°F — likely because the NWS is discounting storm-induced afternoon cooling that models may be handling differently. The META model's output of 84–85°F (57.4%) and 82–83°F (42.6%) appears anomalous and physically implausible given the current observation of 82°F at 8:50 AM with hours of heating ahead; it should be treated with low confidence today.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max at 82°F before 9 AM, a peak around 92–95°F is the most defensible range. A simple 5.5-hour warming window to ~2:30 PM at even a modest 2°F/hr yields ~93°F, consistent with INTRADAY model signals (top bucket 90–91°F) and the NWS's adjusted 95°F call accounting for storm interference. The active even-bucket market's top pick of 96–97°F looks stretched — it would require NWP extremes of 98–103°F to verify AND no meaningful storm cooling, which seems unlikely with 60% precip probability timed exactly at the expected peak window. Confidence is moderate given the storm wildcard.
